en: Victorious is the Sun of the Supreme Ether, who, through his power and accompanied by the goddess Sītā, has arisen to utterly destroy the darkness of fear in those who take refuge in him.
Victory, victory to you, O Great Hero! O Great Sage, leader of the steadfast!
Your boundless majesty was proclaimed by all the gods who assembled during the battle between the gods and the asuras!
O you who were entreated by the assembly of gods humbled by the ten-faced Rāvaṇa to assume the state of the son of Daśaratha;
O sun to the lotus of the Solar dynasty;
O you who fulfilled the final debt of Daśaratha, who was skilled in accompanying the Lord of the Gods in battle!
O you who assumed the guise of a chamberlain in the state of childhood for the sake of the daughter of Kosala! O you who protected Indra’s sacrifice through youthful play!
O hero, foremost in the sacrifice of battle, worthy one, saluted by the multitude of divine weapons!
O you who crush the pride of those who bow before you with the playful grace of your arms;
O destroyer of the frail Tāṭakā and her son Śarāru by the strike of your slender arrows;
O you whose matted hair is thick with the fragments of the moon’s rays; O you who are skilled in the dance upon the crown of the Lord of Dancers!

O Goddess whose feet are as beautiful as the king of lotuses, who wash away the impurities of the world with the abundant flow of the river of the wise, who destroy one's own sins, whose body is as radiant as a flawless gem, and who are praised by the foremost sages and celestial maidens!
O you who are well-known for the ninefold diverse narratives told by the son of Kuśika!

O moon to the cakora-bird eyes of the beautiful-eyed women of the city of Mithilā! O you whose staff-like arms are renowned for shattering the formidable bow of the wielder of the crescent-headed axe (Śiva)!
O you whose eyes plunder the splendor of the white lotus grove awakened by the orb of the fierce sun’s rays!
O you who released the father from the anguish of doubt!
O you who, having avoided the choice of all other kings, sported upon the slopes of Janaka’s daughter’s breasts!
O you whose palms are perfectly formed!

O wielder of the axe, a hundred times harder than a hundred thunderbolts! O supreme sage, you who have drawn your bow with your own hand—a bow difficult even for the mind to bend—and thereby manifested the state of the Supreme Lord!

O destroyer of the sacrifice, you who sport upon mountain peaks; O tormentor of the world, whose fierce deeds surpassed those of Indra; O expert in subduing the ten-faced Rāvaṇa; O lord of a thousand arms, you who filled vast reservoirs with streams of blood from the royal lineages and thereby offered libations.

O you who obstructed the path to a good rebirth for the Lord of the Bhṛgus (Paraśurāma), O you who acted like an iron bar against those who bowed before you, O you whose heart was stolen by the fear of falsehood, O you who were intent on fulfilling the word of your father,
O Prince Regent!

O ocean of noble character, as evidenced by your friendship with the King of Niṣāda! O you who dwell in a delightful abode on the slopes of the wondrous Citrakūṭa mountain, which was taken up for your residence at the command of Bharadvāja!
O You who are not to be instructed by another!
O You who have accomplished the welfare and security of all the worlds through the consecration of Your supreme sandals, firmly set upon the crown-tops of the prostrating Bharata!

O You who crush the power of sins committed by those fond of flesh; O Son who, following the path of the eater of oblations (Agni), acted out of fear when falling upon a blade of grass while lying down in haste; O You whose prowess in great weapons is highly esteemed by all the foremost gods and sages;
O Target of the arrows of Brahmā, Śiva, and Viṣṇu, which are difficult even for them to perceive!
O Daṇḍaka forest, moving Pārijāta tree!
O Virādha, tiger among deer!
You who have scattered the sacrificial rice and grain with many fruits during the commencement of the hunt for nocturnal beasts.
O you who wear the gathered bark garments out of compassion!
O sun that dispels the darkness from the three heads of Triśiras!
O you who dried up the ocean of Dūṣaṇa! O you whose proclamation of victory resounds, having gratified the hosts of sages!
O fierce wind that shatters the groves of the most stubborn thorns! O great elephant-calf that tosses the forest of Nala reeds—the seven thousand demons!
O hero who triumphs without aid!
O fearless one!
O you who are honored! O you whose formidable heroic wounds were caused by the power of the firm embrace of Maithilī, who was delighted at the sight of the great battle!

O you who prepared a thick bed of darbha grass with the skin of the illusory deer of Mārīca; O you whose life was sold for the sake of attaining the glory of valor; O you whose benevolence toward your devotees was manifested by your desire to consume the body of the king of vultures!
O you who assumed the state of a celestial being at the request of Kabandha!
O you whose majesty is never fruitless! O you who purified the heart of the sage-ascetic Śabara through his worship!
O witness to the liberation of Śabarī!
O son of the Wind-god! O you whose heart was delighted by the words of Bhāvuka! O son of the Sun, who made your own sovereignty dependent upon the protection of those who have come for refuge!
You who cast far away the formidable mass of bones from the Dundubhi mountain, as firm as a peak of Mount Kailāsa!
O you whose heart is trusted by friends who tremble at the movement of the big toe of your right foot, which is more agile than Dakṣa’s;
O you who display a wondrous variety of plumage as it suddenly emerges from the gaps between the mountains, the earth, and the vast, wide-spreading trees;
O you who, with the roots of your massive mountain-like arms, firmly crushed Rāvaṇa and produced a thrill of terror that reached the four oceans!

O Lord of the monkey hosts, skilled in dwelling; O you whose heart is vast as the cleaving of a massive stone slab; O you whose arrows are fierce! O you who are born of the swift wind, like a forest fire spreading through enemy cities that are encircled by moats as boundless as the ocean; O best of monkeys, you who have offered all your possessions out of affection!

O Lord of All, whose nature has blossomed through the fury of deceiving various ministers who are like brothers born of an enemy and who have embraced the poison of the Rākṣasa! O You who are consecrated by the vow to protect those who have once taken refuge in You!
O Hero! O observer of the vow of truth!
O you who adorned the sandy banks of the ocean with your reclining place!
O you who dried up the flood of waters in the ocean with the tips of arrows harsh as the fires of universal dissolution;

O you who, with the mountains gathered and carried in the palms of the monkey hosts eager for the sport of fierce battle against powerful enemies, established the boundary of the bridge that divided the sea!

O you whose twang of the bowstring was the instructor in the graceful dance of trembling for the besieged women of Laṅkā, who were like a herd of deer in trees fleeing with swift motion; O you who possess the weight of the golden mountain moving through the sky, who are the embodiment of the Vedas, the very Garuḍa himself, and who have shed the dust of the wind from the wings of Garuḍa!

O you who mangle with arrows like venomous serpents! O you whose eyes are narrowed with disdain at the unprecedented conduct of forest-dwellers in battle! O you who possess the pride and arrogance of wrath, skilled in cleaving the door-like chests of many kinds of Rakshasa army commanders!
O you whose bowstring resounds with a harsh *raṭat* and whose formidable bow twangs with a sharp *ṭaṅkṛti*,
O you of restless and hardy archery! O you whose prowess is renowned for granting rest to the son of Viśravas, who was overwhelmed when his crown was shattered by the strike of your massive arrows!

O you who are like a thunderbolt for shattering the mountain of Kumbhakarṇa’s lineage; O you whose heron-feathered arrows strike fearlessly! O you who, by performing the oblations of the sacrificial fire of black magic, violently shattered the ocean-like waves of the immeasurable monkey army as they fell in haste; O you who caused the younger brother of Indra to cry out in pain upon being struck, witnessed by the gods!
O Rākṣasa, you who engage in duels! You whose prowess is without rival!
You who possess a terrifying display of weapons exceeding even those of Tryambaka!

O charioteer! O you who brought shame to the enemy by seizing his chariot! O you whose majesty was made true before the ten-faced Rāvaṇa, whose ten mouths were cut down by sharp arrows! O you who caused the lotus-forest of Indra’s eyes to tremble with fear as they fell again and again upon seeing the rise of your power! O you for whom a profusion of celestial tree blossoms fell, shimmering with the luster of the sun.

O you who have perfumed the paths of the chariots! O you whose mass of supreme Vedic scriptures is the object of the lamentations of the young women of the night-stalkers— who were rendered helpless by the slaughter produced by the snapping of the ten mouths of the one possessing the most excellent arm-strength that surpasses the entire world!
O best of sages, whose mouth was silenced by the wager;
you who were gladdened by the praises of the lords of the gods, headed by Indra, Agni, Yama, Nirṛti, Varuṇa, Vāyu, Kubera, and Śiva, who had approached you!
O you whose own majesty is known and described by the one of immeasurable intellect; O drop from the ocean of your own power!
O you who have dispelled fear; O you awakened by the wise; O you who lay upon the heroic bed; O you who led the vast host of monkeys!
O you who, at your own appointed time, brought together your well-united consort who shares your heart and dharma!
O you who have brought the sovereignty of Laṅkā under the control of Vibhīṣaṇa!
O you who have accomplished your task! O you who have caused the enemy faction to blossom like a flower in the sky!
O Lord, you who have turned the ocean of the sky into a mere puddle with the impetuous flight of the Puṣpaka chariot;
you who, in a single moment, fulfilled the long-held desire of Bharata by crossing the ocean of the enemy; you who are now enthroned upon the royal throne!

O Rāghava-siṃha! O You whose lotus-feet are illuminated by the mass of rays from the various jewels on the millions of crowns of all kings rolling upon the slopes near Your beautiful footstool, which is like the foothills of the Golden Mountain (Meru)!

O Lord of Ayodhyā, sovereign of the celestial and terrestrial realms! O you who established a righteous royal lineage a hundredfold more prosperous than the ancient dynasty that suffered the slaughter of its kings at the hands of the sage-armed Paraśurāma, enraged by the murder of his father!

O you who delight in pure conduct, O Bharata who have humbled the pride of the hosts of Gandharvas with hundreds of songs of victory; O you who are served by Śatrughna, the subduer of the sons of Madhu;
O you for whom the specific family chronicles are preserved by Kuśa and Lava!
O you who are delighted by listening to the accounts of your own life composed by the best of poets, which transform according to the power of destiny and are the speech of the immortals;
O you who are honored by all people!
O you who gladden Vaiśravaṇa by the gift of excellent celestial palaces restored once more, whose fame is proclaimed in all its splendor;
O nectar that restores to life the young sages who had fallen into the fivefold torments!
O you who, though born in the Tretā Yuga, manifested the conduct of the Kṛta Yuga;
O you who fulfilled the duties of your own caste and stage of life by performing thousands of flawless *Bahusuvarṇaka* horse-sacrifices!
O fulfiller of all actions!
O eternal Dharma!
O you who have manifested as the eternal giver of divine states to the multitude of beings—both the wealthy born in the land of Sāketa and other creatures!
O Sovereign beyond all bounds!
O Blessed Garden for the devotees scorched by the heat of worldly existence!
O Śrī Rāmabhadra!
Homage to you; again, homage to you.
Salutations to Rāma, the householder, who is accompanied by Sītā and who is endowed with sons, grandsons, and so forth, through the mouths of the Lord of Four Faces (Brahmā).
This medicine for the fear of worldly existence, composed by the poet-narrator Siṃha, is difficult yet delicate, with dense and profound compositions.
O wise ones, recite the glory of the Great Hero!
May everything be offered unto Śrī Kṛṣṇa.
